- The run was past this wave's end (07:20Z) when it finished.. Judge: All four pairs are clear calls, and none came close to indistinguishable. The commercial-looking frame wins every time: A in pairs 1 and 2, B in pairs 3 and 4. The in-development frames share one main failure: the world is empty and diagram-like. There is no traffic and there are no pedestrians. Huge flat paver plazas and lawns hold a single cloned acacia-style tree planted on a grid. The towers are generic white boxes and the poles are bare. On top of that, the lighting is flat and evenly washed out, with little directional sun, shadow depth or distance haze; the vegetation looks stylised and toy-like; and the cameras are static, either centred chase shots or top-down views. Their strengths (pleasant skies, decent asphalt and paver textures, boats with wakes, a recognisable landmark skyline) are not enough to read as premium. The winning frames have dense, specific city detail, clear foreground, middle-ground and background layers, backlit haze and sun, convincing car and aircraft materials, and dynamic low or banking camera angles. Only the two hazy, backlit vistas (pair 2 A and pair 4 B) genuinely wowed me. Pair 1 A is hurt by a heavy filter and low resolution. Pair 3 B is lively and rich but lit by plain midday light. The fix that would help the in-development map most is to fill both street-level and aerial views with continuous, varied buildings and life (vehicles, NPCs, street furniture, storefronts). The next priority is a directional sun with haze that builds with distance.
